newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK PETROCHEMICAL, OIL WORKERS BLOCK SHIPMENTS.
newsitem.headline: TURK PETROCHEMICAL, OIL WORKERS BLOCK SHIPMENTS.

text.p: More than 22,000 workers at Turkey's leading state oil and petrochemical plants obstructed shipments from factories on Thursday at the start of a two-day action to force government to accept terms in pay talks, trade union spokesmen said.

"We will not let petrochemicals, gasoline and other petrol products be transported from the factories to the industries or fuel dealers until 5 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Friday," Haci Arap Karadurmus, head of a Petrol-Is branch in central Turkey, told Reuters.
"Action will continue next week if there is no progress in the collective bargaining negotiations," he added.

The protest took place in a total of 13 plants belonging to Petkim Petrokimya Holding A.S., Tupras Turkiye Petrol Rafinerileri A.S., Turkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortakligi (TPAO), Petrol Ofisi A.S. and Botas Boru Tasimaciligi A.S.
The plants are mainly located in the western and southern coastal regions of the country.
"Our 22,000 members will not leave their work sites and we will take effective actions on production, sales and shipments," Bayram Yildirim, president of Petrol-Is, told Reuters.
"If there is no progress in the talks, we will attempt to halt production at these plants next week," he said.

Petrol-Is officials urge the government to take steps towards an accord to end pay talks continuing since February between the cabinet and trade union confederation Turk-Is representing more than 500,000 public workers.
Turk-Is, the biggest confederation in Turkey, and the government have not resolved disputes in the negotiations for a two-year labour contract from January 1 1997.
The action was also enforced in western Kocaeli town where the biggest refinery and petrochemical facilities are, Ali Bugdayci, head of Petrol-Is Kocaeli/Korfez branch, told Reuters.

Petrol-Is which operates in major oil related industries also wants to sign separate labour contracts with the government because of the special characteristics of the sector, like Hava-Is, active in the aviation industry led by national carrier Turk Hava Yollari.
Hava-Is signed a two-year labour contract with Turkish Airlines on Thursday, independently of Turk-Is.
